title: A Word to the Bridegroom and Bride
attribution_note: Translated for this edition from the Russian of St John of Kronstadt (1829-1908, public domain), his Слово жениху и невесте, a sermon addressed to a couple at their wedding. Russian text: https://www.sobor.de/ (Cathedral of the Holy New Martyrs and Confessors of Russia, Munich).

pairs.en: Honorable bridegroom and honorable bride! You come to the great mystery called marriage. Great, because the union of husband and wife pictures the most holy union of Jesus Christ with the Church — that is, with believers in Him. As the husband is head of the wife, so Christ is head of the Church [Eph. 5:23]. As bridegroom and bride are crowned in marriage into one flesh, so Christ and His Church are also one body, for those who truly believe in Him are members... of His body, of His flesh and of His bones [Eph. 5:30].

sections.heading: The duties of a holy marriage

pairs.en:
This great mystery of marriage lays great duties on you both, which you must strive to fulfil with all your might. Your life together must be pure and holy, as holy as the Lord's union with the Church. It must be thoughtful, loving, peaceful, and unbreakable. Your life together must be pure and holy, for the Lord Himself, who created man in the beginning, male and female, joins husband and wife into one flesh, for mutual help in bodily and spiritual needs, and to increase the human race.
The purpose is high and holy: from now on you become living instruments of Divine goodness and almightiness, for through husband and wife the all-good Creator calls rational creatures to being and life — His future children and heirs of the Kingdom of God. And if the Lord blesses you with children, you must raise them in Orthodox faith and Christian life, being first an example to them of faith, piety, and fear of God. And to each other you must be an example of gentleness, kindness, self-control, good cheer, honesty, hard work, submission to God's will, patience, and hope. Help each other. Cherish each other. Yield to one another, covering each other's weaknesses with love.

There are unhappy marriages too. Sometimes husband and wife come together as if only for their sin and misery. Why are they unhappy? Mostly from clashing characters, from not giving way to each other. From a husband's stubbornness, self-will, fault-finding, or his reckless temper. From unfaithfulness of husband or wife. From a husband's intemperance or gambling. From a wife's love of fine clothes, her wilfulness, malice, quarrelsomeness, stubbornness, from not bearing life's lacks. May the Lord help you avoid such sinful life together and such marital miseries.

Keep always faith and fear of God in your heart. Good sense, patience, hope. Work and pray. Go to bed and rise with prayer in your heart and on your lips. Do not miss church gatherings. Earnestly fulfil your Christian duty of confession and communion of the Holy Mysteries of Christ. In these sacraments you will find, apart from grace of cleansing of sins and hallowing of soul and body, grace of firm unity, hallowing of the very loins and of the womb of the coming generation, renewal of spiritual and bodily strength, help, comfort, and encouragement in life's hard circumstances, healing of illnesses.

Your life together must be thoughtful, for holy apostle Peter says: You husbands, dwell with your wives with understanding, as with the weaker vessel, giving them honor as fellow heirs of the gracious life, that your prayers be not hindered [1 Pet. 3:7].

sections.heading: Strangers on earth, bound for heaven

pairs.en: And you must always understand why the Lord has joined you in the bonds of marriage, having crowned you into one flesh. You must never stop seeking together the Kingdom of God. And if God gives children, you must raise them too, and prepare them chiefly for eternal blessings. Temporal blessings are deceptive, brief, and not life's goal. Christians are promised blessings unfading, spiritual, eternal. Spur each other to God's love, heavenly blessings, and neighbor-love. Keeping heaven always in view, you must count yourselves strangers and sojourners on earth. Value time and spend it on deeds of righteousness, not on empty, vain, and sinful deeds. Count each day a great gift of God's mercy, given us for turning to God, for amendment, for grounding and growth in virtue, for saving the soul. Redeeming the time, because the days are evil [Eph. 5:16].

sections.heading: Love, peace, and an unbreakable bond

pairs.en:
Your life together must be loving and peaceful. Can it be otherwise? No one ever hated his own flesh, but feeds and warms it, as the Lord does the Church. Henceforth you shall be one flesh. A husband must love his wife as his own body, for he who loves his wife loves himself [Eph. 5:29–28]. If you love each other, you will draw God's grace down on yourselves and your children. God will dwell in you and crown all your undertakings with blessed success. For where love is, there is God; and where God is, there is everything good. With love, peace will settle in your home, for love suffers long and covers all things, and does not let a person be irritated, angry, wilful, or hurtful in word or deed.
At last, your life together must be unbreakable — to the grave. Christian love loves unto the end, not for a time. It is firm and constant. Trials will come for your love, from one or the other's weakness, from clashing characters or habits, from others, from the ancient enemy. Overcome these trials with courage. Be wise as serpents, simple as doves [Matt. 10:16]. Be not irritated. Be patient. Yield. Strengthen yourselves in faith in Christ Jesus, who shall be to you, honorable bridegroom and honorable bride, ever example of holy love, gentleness, kindness, patience — your strength, your light and Guide, your Defender and Savior to the grave. Amen.
St. John of Kronstadt
